subject: Request: LLM custody, no-adaptive-learning commitment & subprocessor/cross-border assurances
messages:
From: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acmehealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-10-30T09:12:00Z
Subject: LLM processing assurances and no-training request

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week. Before we can move to procurement, legal needs clarity on three things for our DPA:

1) A firm commitment that Acme Health interaction data will not be used to improve models (no adaptive training) unless we explicitly opt in.
2) Which subprocessors you rely on for processing and storage, and whether those subprocessors will transfer any data outside the EU.
3) Confirmation of prompt/response custody: we need to guarantee that prompt content and model outputs generated for our tenant are only accessible to us and are not treated as Redwood IP or used as training signal.

Can you share a short summary we can attach to our procurement packet? Also note we may require an onshore-processing addendum (EU-only) and KMS residency for encryption keys.

Best,
Sarah Lee
Senior Counsel, Acme Health

---
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acmehealth.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-30T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: LLM processing assurances and no-training request

Hi Sarah — really appreciate the clear list. High level answers below; legal and ops are copied in to confirm details and provide artifacts.

Quick summary for procurement (draft):
- No-adaptive-training: Redwood will commit that customer data from Acme Health will not be used to train or improve any Redwood models (no adaptive training) unless Acme signs an explicit opt-in amendment.
- Prompt/Response custody: Acme retains ownership of prompts and outputs. Redwood will not assert rights over customer prompts/responses and will not license outputs for model training.
- Subprocessors & cross-border: Primary processing for your EU tenant will be restricted to our EU region (GCP europe-west1). We will provide a list of subprocessors and an attestation of any cross-border transfers; in our proposed configuration logs and telemetry can be routed to EU-only storage.

Next steps we propose:
1) Ops to provide a processing diagram + subprocessor list (see attachment).
2) Legal to propose DPA amendment language for the no-train and custody commitments.
3) We send a DocuSign amendment for signature.

David / Kimberly — can you confirm the subprocessor list, KMS residency options, and whether we can commit to EU-only logging for this tenant?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Lead | Redwood Inference

---
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-30T11:22:00Z
Subject: RE: LLM processing assurances and no-training request

Marissa / Sarah — ops check-in. Attached is a simple diagram showing the proposed EU-only architecture (20271030-ops-eu-processing-diagram.png). Key points:

- Compute & model serving: GCP europe-west1 (no failover to other regions for this tenant unless explicitly enabled).
- Storage: Customer prompt and output records can be stored in EU buckets with retention configurable by Acme. Default is 30 days, but we can set 0-day retention for ephemeral use (delete after response) if required.
- KMS: We can offer customer-managed keys in an EU KMS (bring-your-own-key option) or host-managed keys that are region-bound.
- Subprocessors: current list for EU deployment:
  * Google Cloud (europe-west1) — compute & storage
  * LogSafe Inc. (eu-logging service) — optional, EU-only logging if enabled
  * SentryOps (error telemetry) — EU-only configuration available
- Telemetry & telemetry ingestion: we can gate PII out of telemetry and route non-PII metrics to EU logging.

We can produce a signed subprocessors attestation and a short Ops-runbook for the onboarding packet. Attaching diagram and will export the subprocessor inventory as a CSV for legal.

Attachments: 20271030-ops-eu-processing-diagram.png (ops diagram)

-David
David Kim
Head of Infra Operations | Redwood Inference

---
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acmehealth.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-30T13:40:00Z
Subject: RE: LLM processing assurances and no-training request

Thanks — quick legal draft notes for procurement packet. Marissa, happy to refine:

Proposed DPA amendment language (summary):
- No adaptive training: "Redwood shall not use Customer Data (including prompts and generated outputs) to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve any machine learning models owned or operated by Redwood, unless Customer has provided an explicit, written opt-in that specifies scope and duration."
- Ownership/custody: "Customer retains exclusive ownership of Customer Data, including prompts and generated outputs. Redwood does not acquire any rights to exploit Customer Data for model improvement, product development, or marketing."
- Subprocessor & cross-border: "Redwood will process Customer Data within the EU region for the Acme tenant. If Redwood intends to engage a subprocessor outside the EU, Redwood will provide 30 days' prior written notice and obtain Customer's consent for transfers that are not covered by a standard contractual clause or equivalent safeguards."

Open/legal asks:
- Do we need to add an escrow or exportability guarantee for outputs? (some enterprise customers ask for daily export snapshots)
- Can ops guarantee zero-copy retention (i.e., ephemeral KV usage with no persistent logs) for the pilot? If not, we should offer explicit retention windows.

I will prepare a DPA amendment doc and mark configurable fields (retention, KMS choice, subprocessor gating). Once Marissa confirms, we'll route for signature via DocuSign.

-Kimberly Park
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Security | Redwood Inference

---
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acmehealth.com>, Ben Hughes <ben.hughes@acmehealth.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-30T16:05:00Z
Subject: Re: LLM processing assurances and no-training request

Hi Sarah / Ben — attaching a short packet you can include with procurement:

- Ops diagram (20271030-ops-eu-processing-diagram.png) — shows EU-only compute and optional EU-only logging.
- Draft DPA amendment (20271030-dpa-amendment-draft.docx) — includes no-adaptive-training and ownership language (Kimberly's draft above).
- Subprocessor inventory (CSV) — exported to your request, will deliver separately in the next hour.

Summary of commitments we will include in the amendment:
1) No adaptive training without explicit opt-in.
2) Customer retains ownership of prompts & outputs; Redwood will not use them for model improvement.
3) EU-only processing for the Acme tenant by default; any non-EU processing requires notice and consent.
4) KMS options: customer-managed EU KMS or region-bound Redwood-managed keys.
5) Telemetry will be scrubbed for PII and can be routed to EU-only logging; logging is optional.

Next steps: If that aligns with Acme's checklist, Kimberly will finalize the DPA amendment and we will send via DocuSign. For procurement references: HubSpot deal HS-45231.

DocuSign (provisional link): https://www.docusign.com/en/documents/ACME-Amendment-45231

Would you like us to include a one-week export of outputs as an onboarding snapshot into your custody during pilot? That can help with escrow concerns.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Lead | Redwood Inference
